0.zh: 第一部分　客观逻辑

en: The complete transformation which the philosophical mode of thinking has undergone among us for the last twenty-five years or so, and the higher standpoint which the self-consciousness of Spirit has attained over itself in this period, have so far had little influence upon the shape of logic.
zh: 近二十五年来，哲学的思维方式在我们中间所经历的彻底改变，以及精神在这一时期通过自我意识而在自身之上达到的更高立场，迄今对逻辑学的形态还很少产生影响。

en: What was called metaphysics before this period has, so to speak, been eradicated root and branch and has vanished from the series of the sciences.
Where are the voices of the former ontology, of rational psychology, of cosmology, or even of the former natural theology still to be heard, or where may they still be heard?
Investigations, for example, into the immateriality of the soul, into the mediating causes and the final causes, where should they still find an interest?
The other proofs of the existence of God are likewise adduced only historically, or for the sake of edification and elevation of the mind.
It is a fact that the interest in the former metaphysics has been lost, partly in its content, partly in its form, and partly in both at once.

As remarkable as it is when a people has become unable to use the science of its state law, when its convictions, its ethical customs and virtues have become useless to it, so remarkable is it at least when a people loses its metaphysics, when the Spirit, occupied with its own pure essence, no longer has any actual existence in it.
zh: 在这个时期之前被称作形而上学的东西，可以说已被连根拔除，从科学的行列中消失了。
从前的本体论、理性心理学、宇宙论，乃至从前的自然神学的声音，还能从哪里发出，又还能从哪里被听到呢？
例如关于灵魂非物质性的研究，关于中介原因与终极原因的研究，它们还能在哪里找到兴趣呢？
其余关于上帝的存在的证明，同样只是出于历史的考虑，或者为了感化与提升心灵而被援引。
这是一个事实：对从前形而上学的兴趣，无论是就其内容、就其形式，还是就两者同时而言，都已失去。
一个民族若对自己的国家法科学、对自己的信念、伦理习俗与德性都已不再适用，那是值得注意的；而一个民族若失去了自己的形而上学，专注于自身纯粹本质的精神在其中不再有任何现实的定在，那至少同样是值得注意的。

en: The exoteric doctrine of the Kantian philosophy — that the understanding must not soar beyond experience, otherwise the faculty of cognition becomes theoretical reason, which for its own part engenders nothing but brain-spun phantasms — has justified, from the scientific side, the renunciation of speculative thinking.

Against this popular doctrine there were the cries of modern pedagogy and the necessity of the times, which direct the gaze to immediate need, maintaining that just as experience is the first thing for cognition, so for skill in public and private life theoretical insight is even harmful, and exercise and practical formation are in general the essential and only thing that promotes.

— Thus, science and the common sense of ordinary men working hand in hand to bring about the downfall of metaphysics, it seemed that the strange spectacle was being brought about of seeing a cultivated people without metaphysics, like a temple otherwise most variously adorned but without the Holy of Holies.

— The theology which in earlier times was the keeper of the speculative mysteries and of the although dependent metaphysics had abandoned this science in favour of feelings, in favour of the practical and popular, and of learned history.

Corresponding to this change is the fact that elsewhere those solitaries who were sacrificed by their people and removed from the world disappeared, to the end that contemplation of the eternal and a life devoted to it alone might exist — not for the sake of any benefit, but for the sake of blessing; a disappearance which, in another connection, can in its essence be regarded as the same appearance as the one just mentioned.

— So that, after the driving out of this darkness, of this colourless occupation of the Spirit turned back upon itself, existence seemed to be transformed into the cheerful world of flowers, among which, as is well known, there is no black one.
zh: 康德哲学的外显学说——即知性不得飞越经验，否则认识能力就变成理论理性，而理论理性本身只能生出头脑编织出来的幻影——从科学这一面为放弃思辨的思维作了辩护。
与这种流行学说相抗衡的，是现代教育学的叫嚷，是那把目光投向直接需要的时代的必需：它主张，正如对认识来说经验是第一位的，那么对公共生活与私人生活中的灵巧来说，理论洞察甚至是有害的，而练习与实际教养才是根本上唯一有促进作用的。
——这样，科学与常人的常识携手促成形而上学的覆亡，仿佛一场奇特的景观被促成了：看到一个有教养的民族竟没有形而上学——就像一座原本装饰得绚丽多彩的庙宇却缺少了至圣所。
——神学在早期时代本是思辨的奥秘与虽属依附的形而上学的守护者，然而它已经放弃了这门科学，转向了情感，转向了实践与通俗的一面，转向了有学问的历史。
与这一变化相应的是：别处那些被自己民族献祭、被逐出世界的孤独者消失了，其目的是使对永恒者的沉思以及一种只侍奉它的生活得以存在——不是为了任何功利，而是为了福祉；这种消失在另一种关联中，就其本质而言，可以看作与刚才所说的同一现象。
——于是，在这些黑暗被驱逐之后，在精神转身向内的无色忙碌被驱逐之后，定在仿佛已被转化为花朵的明朗世界，而在这些花里，众所周知是没有黑色的。

en: The fate of logic has not been much better than that of metaphysics.

The prejudice that one learns through logic to think what otherwise was regarded as useful for it, and thereby for its purpose — as though one first had to learn to digest and to move through the study of anatomy and physiology — has long since been lost, and the spirit of the practical had probably assigned logic no better fate than that of its sister.
Nevertheless, probably for the sake of some formal advantage, a rank among the sciences was still left to it; indeed it was even retained as a subject of public instruction.

This better lot, however, concerns only the external fate; for its shape and content have remained the same as what was handed down through a long tradition, but had in this transmission become more and more diluted and emaciated; the new Spirit which has arisen, not less upon the science than upon actuality, has not yet been felt in it.

But it is altogether in vain, when the substantial form of the Spirit has changed itself, to want to preserve the forms of earlier formation; they are withered leaves, which are shaken off by the new buds which are already forming at their roots.
zh: 逻辑学的命运并不比形而上学的命运好到哪里去。
认为要通过逻辑学才能学会思考那些原本被看作对逻辑学有用、并因而对它的目的有用的东西——就仿佛人必须先通过研究解剖学与生理学，才能学会消化与运动——这种成见早已消失；而务实的精神大概也不会给逻辑学安排比它姊妹更好的命运。
尽管如此，大概是为了某种形式上的益处，逻辑学在诸科学之中仍被保留了一个位次；它甚至被作为公共教学的一门科目保留了下来。
不过，这个较好的命运只涉及外在的命运；因为它的形态与内容仍旧是那个通过悠久的传统传承下来的东西，只不过在传承中变得越来越稀薄、越来越干瘪；那个在科学上并不少于在现实性上已经涌现的新精神，尚未在它身上显露出来。
然而，当精神的实体形式已经改变自身之后，还想保留早先形成的那些形式，是一劳永逸地徒劳的；它们是枯萎的叶子，会被那些已经在其根部生成的新芽抖落。

en: With the ignoring of the general change, it is beginning to happen, little by little, even in the matter of science.

Unnoticed, the other representations have even become familiar and proper to the opponents themselves; and if they continue to act brittle towards their source and principles and behave towards them in a self-contradictory way, they have submitted to the consequences and have been unable to ward off their influence; for their negative behaviour, which keeps becoming more insignificant, they know no other way of giving themselves a positive importance and content than by joining in with the new modes of representation.
zh: 随着对这一普遍变化的漠视，即使在科学领域里，也开始渐渐地出现这种情况。
在不知不觉中，就连反对者也已熟悉并习惯了别的表象；当他们仍旧对那些表象的来源与原则显得僵硬、并且自相矛盾地反对它们时，他们已经接受了这些后果，并且无法抵挡它们的影响；由于他们那越来越无足轻重的否定态度，他们除了在新表象方式中插话之外，再没有别的办法为自己赢得积极的重要性与内容。

en: On the other hand, it seems that the time of fermentation, with which a new creation begins, is past.

In its first appearance such a time is accustomed to behave with fanatical hostility towards the widespread systematization of the earlier principle, partly also to be afraid of losing itself in the extension of the particular, partly however to shun the labour required for scientific formation and, in need of one, to have recourse at once to an empty formalism.
The demand for the working up and formation of the material now becomes ever more urgent.
It is a period in the formation of an age, as in the formation of the individual, in which it is above all about the acquisition and the assertion of the principle in its undeveloped intensity.
But the higher requirement is directed toward its becoming science.
zh: 从另一方面看，那种孕育着新创造的发酵时期似乎已经过去了。
这种时期在最初出现时，惯于以狂热的敌意对待早已铺开的对先前原则的体系化；有时它也害怕在特殊性的扩展中迷失自己，有时又躲避科学陶冶所必需的工作，而在需要它的时候，一开始就抓住一种空洞的形式主义。
于是，对材料的加工与陶冶的要求变得越来越迫切。
这这是一个时代的形成期，正如个体的形成期一样，在这里首要的在于获取原则，并在它尚未展开的强度上加以主张。
但更高的要求指向的是：它要成为科学。

en: Whatever may already have been done for the subject matter and the form of the science in other respects, the logical science, which constitutes the proper metaphysics or pure speculative philosophy, has so far been very much neglected.
What I understand more precisely by this science and its standpoint, I have indicated provisionally in the Introduction.

The necessity of beginning afresh with this science once more, the nature of the subject itself, and the want of preparatory works which might have been used for the transformation undertaken, may be taken into account by cheap judgements, even though a many years' labour could not give this attempt a greater perfection.
— The essential point of view is that the question is at all about a new conception of scientific treatment.

Philosophy, in so far as it is to be science, cannot, as I have remarked elsewhere1, borrow its method for this from a subordinate science such as mathematics, any more than it can content itself with categorical assertions of inner intuition or use ratiocination on grounds of external reflection.
Rather, it can only be the nature of the content which moves in scientific cognition; for it is this own reflection of the content which at the same time first posits and produces its determination.
zh: 无论就这门科学的对象与形式而言此前在其他方面已经做了些什么，逻辑科学——它构成真正的形而上学或纯粹思辨哲学——迄今都还大大地被忽略了。
我对这门科学及其立场更确切的理解，已在《导言》中作了初步的说明。
不得不再次从头开始处理这门科学的必然性、对象本身的性质，以及本可用于这次改造的前期工作之缺乏，这些都可以由轻率的评判者来权衡，尽管多年的努力也未能使这次尝试达到更高的完善。
——根本的着眼点在于：问题归根结底是关于科学处理的一种新概念。
哲学既然应当是科学，就不能像我在别处指出的那样，为此从一门从属的科学（数学就是这样的科学）借取其方法，同样也不能满足于对内在直观的断言式担保，或出于外在反思的缘故而诉诸推理。
而只能是内容的性质在科学认识中运动；因为正是内容自身的这种反思，才同时首先设定并产生出这一规定。

en: The understanding determines and holds fast the determinations; reason is negative and dialectical, because it dissolves the determinations of the understanding into nothing; it is positive because it produces the universal and comprehends the particular in it.
Just as the understanding is generally taken as something separate from reason, so the dialectical reason is also usually taken as something separate from the positive reason.
But in its truth reason is Spirit, which is higher than both, intelligible reason or rational understanding.

It is the negative, that which constitutes the quality both of dialectical reason and of the understanding; — it negates the simple, and so it posits the determinate difference of the understanding; it dissolves that difference just as much, and so it is dialectical.

But it does not remain in the nothing of this result, but is just as positive in it and has thereby established the first simple, but as a universal which is concrete in itself; under this, no given particular is subsumed, but in that determination and in the dissolution of the same the particular has already determined itself along with it.

This spiritual movement, which in its simplicity gives itself its determinateness and in this determinateness its equality with itself, and which is thereby the immanent development of the concept, is the absolute method of cognition and at the same time the immanent soul of the content itself.
— On this self-constructing path alone, I assert, philosophy is capable of being objective, demonstrated science.
— In this way I have attempted to present consciousness in the Phenomenology of Spirit.

Consciousness is Spirit as concrete knowledge, and indeed knowledge entangled in externality; but the onward movement of this subject rests, like the development of all natural and spiritual life, solely on the nature of the pure essences which constitute the content of logic.

Consciousness, as the appearing Spirit which frees itself on its way from its immediacy and external determinacy, becomes pure knowledge, which makes those pure essences themselves, as they are in and for themselves, its object.
They are the pure thoughts, the Spirit which thinks its essence.
Their self-movement is their spiritual life and is that by which science constitutes itself and of which it is the exposition.
zh: 知性规定并固定这些规定；理性是否定而辩证的，因为它把知性的规定化解为无；理性又是肯定的，因为它产生普遍者，并在其中以概念把握特殊者。
正像人们通常把知性看作与理性相分离的东西一样，人们也惯于把辩证的理性看作与肯定的理性相分离的东西。
但就其真理而言，理性是精神，是高于二者的东西，是可理解的理性或合乎理性的知性。
它是否定者，是构成辩证理性与知性两者的质的东西；——它否定单纯者，于是它设定知性的规定差别；它同样消解这一差别，于是它是辩证的。
但它并不停留于这一结果的空无之中，而是在其中同样是肯定的；这样它就建立起第一个单纯者，但这个单纯者是一个在自身具体的普遍者；在它之下并不是把一个现成的特殊者归摄进去，而是在那种规定与对它的消解之中，特殊者本身已经随之得到规定。
这种精神的运动在其单纯性中赋予自身以规定性，并在这一规定性中赋予自身以同自身的同一；它因此就是概念的内在发展，是认识的绝对方法，同时也是内容自身的内在灵魂。
——我主张，只有在这条自我构造的道路上，哲学才有能力成为客观的、经过论证的科学。
——我曾试图以这样的方式，在《精神现象学》中呈现意识。
意识是精神，作为具体的、因而在外在性中受局限的知识；但这一对象的推进却单单——正如一切自然生活与精神生活的发展一样——建立在构成逻辑学内容的纯粹本质的性质之上。
意识作为显现的精神，在其行程中从自身的直接性与外在的具体性中解放出来，成为纯粹的知识，它把那些纯粹本质本身——如它们自在自为的那样——当作自己的对象。
它们是纯粹的思想，是那个以思维为本质的精神。
它们的自我运动就是它们的精神生命，是科学借以自我构成的东西，也是科学所表述的东西。

en: The relation of the science which I call the Phenomenology of Spirit to logic is hereby indicated.

— As for the external relation, the first part of the system of science2, which contains the Phenomenology, was destined to be followed by a second part, which was to contain logic and the two real sciences of philosophy, the philosophy of nature and the philosophy of Spirit, and would have concluded the system of science.

But the necessary expansion which logic had to obtain for itself has induced me to let it come to the fore especially; it therefore constitutes in an extended plan the first sequel to the Phenomenology of Spirit.
Later I shall let the treatment of the two real sciences of philosophy just named follow.

— This first volume of logic contains, as its first book, the doctrine of Being, the second book, the doctrine of Essence, as the second division of the first volume; the second volume will contain subjective logic or the doctrine of the Concept.
zh: 至此，我称之为《精神现象学》的这门科学与逻辑学的关系已经说明。
——就外在关系而言，这门科学的体系2的第一部分（其中包含《精神现象学》）原定要有一个第二部分跟上，那一部分应当包含逻辑学以及哲学的两门实在的科学——自然哲学与精神哲学——并以此结束整个科学的体系。
但逻辑学为自身所必需的扩展促使我让它特别地显露出来；于是在一个扩充了的计划中，它便构成了对《精神现象学》的第一部续篇。
此后我将继续处理上面提到的哲学的两门实在的科学。
——逻辑学的这第一卷以第一篇包含存在的学说，以第二篇即本质的学说作为第一卷的第二部分；第二卷则将包含主观逻辑，即概念的学说。

en: Nuremberg, 22. March 1812
zh: 纽伦堡，1812 年 3 月 22. 日

en: I have undertaken this new treatment of the science of logic, of which the first volume now appears, fully aware both of the difficulty of the subject in itself and then of its exposition, as well as of the incompleteness which the treatment of it in the first edition carries with it; although after further many years' occupation with this science I had striven to remedy this incompleteness, I still feel I have good reason to claim the indulgence of the reader.
A title of such a claim may indeed in the first place be grounded on the circumstance that for the content one has found in the earlier metaphysics and logic only external material.

However generally and frequently the same has been worked on — the latter continued right up to our own times — so little did such treatment touch the speculative side; rather, on the whole, the same material has been repeated, alternately now diluted to trivial superficiality, now fetched up anew and dragged along with it the old ballast in greater bulk, so that through such, often quite merely mechanical, labours no gain could accrue to the philosophical content.

To present the realm of thought philosophically, i.e. in its own immanent activity or, what is the same, in its necessary development, must therefore have been a new undertaking and had to be begun from the very beginning; that acquired material, those known forms of thought, must, however, be regarded as a most important template, indeed a necessary condition and a premise to be gratefully acknowledged, even if it only gives here and there a thin thread or the lifeless bones of a skeleton, even thrown together disorderly among themselves.
zh: 我着手重新处理逻辑学这门科学——现在呈现出来的是它的第一卷——时，完全意识到两方面的难处：对象本身的困难以及它的表述，还有第一版对它的处理所带有的那种不完善；尽管在进一步钻研这门学问的多年之后，我曾努力想弥补这种不完善，我仍然感到自己有充分理由请求读者的宽容。
而书名所作的这种要求，首先大概可以建立在这样的情形之上：在早先的形而上学与逻辑学中，人们为内容找到的主要只是外在的材料。
同样的材料被如此普遍而频繁地加工着——后者一直延续到我们的时代——却如此少地触及思辨的一面；相反，整体上被重复的始终是同一份材料，时而稀薄到流于琐屑的表面化，时而又把旧有的重负重新更大规模地翻出来并拖带着，以致通过这些往往纯属机械的劳作，哲学内容不可能有任何增长。
因此，要在哲学的意义上——即在思想自身的内在活动中，或在它必然的发展中——把思想的领域表述出来，就必定是一项全新的事业，而且必须从头做起；不过，那些已经获取的材料、那些为人熟知的思维形式，却应当被视为一份极其重要的底本，乃至一个必要条件、一个应当心存感激地予以承认的前提，即使它所能提供的不过是些稀疏的线头或一副骨架的无生命的骨头，甚至是被杂乱无章地堆在一起的。

en: The forms of thought are first of all set forth and deposited in the language of man; in our days it cannot be reminded often enough that that whereby man is distinguished from the animal is thinking.

Into everything which becomes an inner thing for him, a representation at all, whatever he makes his own, language has pressed itself; and whatever he makes into language and expresses in it contains a category, whether wrapped up, mixed in, or worked out; so very natural is the logical to him, or rather: that very thing is his peculiar nature itself.

But if one confronts nature in general, as the physical, with the spiritual, one would have to say that the logical is rather the supernatural, which presses into all the natural behaviour of man, into his feeling, his intuiting, his desiring, his needing, his urging, and thereby makes it at all into something human — even if only formally — into representations and purposes.

It is an advantage of a language when it possesses a wealth of logical expressions, namely proper and separated ones, for the determinations of thought themselves; of the prepositions and articles many already belong to such relations as are based on thinking; the Chinese language is said not to have reached that at all in its development, or only scantily; but these particles appear quite in the service, only a little more detached than the augmentations, the inflectional signs and the like.

Far more important is it that in a language the determinations of thought are set out as nouns and verbs and are thus stamped into an objective form; the German language has in this many advantages over the other modern languages; indeed some of its words have the further peculiarity of having not only different meanings but opposite ones, so that a speculative spirit of the language is not to be unrecognized in it; it can afford the thinking a pleasure to come upon such words and to find the unification of opposites — which result of speculation is yet nonsense for the understanding — already lexically, in a naive fashion, presented as one word with opposite meanings.

Philosophy therefore needs no special terminology at all; a few words are indeed to be taken over from foreign languages, which however have already acquired citizenship in it through use; — an affected purism would be least in place precisely where the matter itself is most at stake.

— The advance of formation in general, and especially of the sciences, even the empirical and sensible ones, in so far as they move in general in the most ordinary categories (e.g. of a whole and its parts, of a thing and its properties and the like), gradually also brings to light higher relations of thought, or at least lifts them up to greater universality and thereby to closer attention.

If, for example, in physics the determination of thought of force has become predominant, then in recent times the category of polarity — which, incidentally, has intruded far too much à tort et à travers into everything, even into light — plays the most significant role, — the determination of a difference in which the different are inseparably united; that in this way one proceeds from the form of abstraction, of identity, through which a determinacy such as force gains a self-sufficiency, and that the form of determination, of difference, which at the same time remains as an inseparable in identity, is lifted out and has become a current representation, is of infinite importance.

The consideration of nature brings with it, through the reality in which its objects hold fast, this compulsion: to fix the categories which can no longer be ignored in it, even if with the greatest inconsistency towards others which are also allowed to hold, and not to permit that, as happens more easily in the spiritual, one passes over to abstractions from the opposition and to generalities.
zh: 思维形式首先是在人的语言中被树立并安放下来的；在我们今天的日子里，再怎么反复提醒也不为过：使人与动物相区别的东西就是思维。
语言已经渗入到他使之成为内在的、成为某种表象的一切东西之中，即他据为己有的一切东西之中；而他使之成为语言并在语言中表达出来的一切，无论是被包裹着的、混杂着的，还是被提炼出来的，都包含着一个范畴；逻辑的东西对他来说是如此自然，或者更确切地说：这个东西本身就是他的独特本性。
但如果把自然整体、作为物理的东西，与精神相对立起来，那就必须说，逻辑的东西毋宁是超自然的东西：它渗入人的一切自然行为，渗入他的感受、直观、欲求、需要与冲动，并由此使它总体上成为属人的东西——哪怕只是形式上的——成为表象与目的。
一门语言若自身为思维规定备有一份逻辑表达的财富——即专属于思维规定、与之分开的表达——那就是这门语言的优势；在介词与冠词之中，已经有许多属于以思维为基础的那些关系；据说汉语在其发展中对这一点根本没有达到，或者只达到微薄的程度；但这些虚词完全是服役性地出现，只比那些增音前缀、屈折标记之类稍稍分离一些而已。

更为重要的是：在一门语言中，思维规定被树立为名词和动词，并因此被打上客观形式的印记；德语在这方面比别的现代语言有许多长处；甚至它有些词还具有一种进一步的特性——不仅有多种意义，而且有相反的意义——以致一种思辨的精神——语言的精神——在那里本身是不可错认的；思维遇到这样的词时会感到愉悦，因为对立者的统一——这一思辨的结果对知性来说还是荒谬的——在这里已经以朴素的词书方式被当作一个具有相反意义的词呈现出来了。
因此哲学根本不需要专门的术语；诚然要从外来语言中采纳一些词，但这些词通过使用已经在那门语言里取得了公民权；——一种矫揉造作的纯粹主义，恰恰在最关系到事情本身的地方最不相宜。
——形成过程本身的推进，特别是科学的推进——即便那些经验的与感性的科学——因为它们总体上是在最普通的范畴中活动的（例如整体与部分、事物及其属性之类），也会逐渐把更高的思维关系带到光天化日之下，或者至少把它们提升到更大的普遍性、因而提升到更密切的注意。

比如说，如果物理学中思维规定「力」取得了支配地位，那么近来人极性这一范畴——它此外已经过分地 à tort et à travers 地侵入了一切，甚至侵入光——就扮演着最重要的角色；——即对这样一个差别的规定，在这一差别中相异者是不可分地联系着的；从抽象的形式、同一性的形式出发（力这一规定性正是通过它获得自身的独立性），并把规定性的形式、即差别的形式——它同时作为不可分者留在同一性之中——提升出来而成为通行的表象，这一过程具有无穷的重要性。
自然考察通过其对象据以持存的实在性，带来了这种强制性：把其中已不能再被漠视的范畴固定下来，即便对另一些同样被容许保留的范畴表现出极大的不一致；并且不容许像在精神领域里较为容易发生的那样，转向对对立面的抽象并走向普遍性。

en: But although the logical objects and their expressions are roughly well known in formation, what is known is for that reason not known, as I have said elsewhere; and it can even arouse impatience that one should still have to occupy oneself with what is already known, — and what is better known than precisely those determinations of thought of which we make use everywhere, which issue from our mouths in every sentence we speak?

This preface is destined to indicate the general moments of the course of cognition starting from this known, and of the relation of scientific thinking to this natural thinking; so much, taken together with what the earlier Introduction contains, will be sufficient to give a general conception of the sense of logical cognition, such a conception as one demands to have in advance of a science — in advance of the science which is the thing itself.
zh: 不过，虽然逻辑的对象及其表达在形成中大致是众所周知的，但如我在别处所说，众所周知的东西正因此并没有被认识；而且甚至会引起不耐烦：人们还得去从事那众所周知的东西；——而还有什么比思维规定更众所周知呢？我们在各处都使用它们，它们在我们所说的每一句话里都从我们口中溜出来。
本序言的任务，正是要指出从这一已知者出发的认识进程的一般环节，指出科学的思维与这种自然的思维之间的关系的一般环节；这些内容，连同早先《导言》所包含的内容一起，将足以给出关于逻辑认识之意味的一种总体表象——那种人们在一门科学之前、即在作为事情本身的那门科学之前所要求的总体表象。

en: First of all, it is to be regarded as an infinite advance that the forms of thought have been freed from the material in which they are immersed in self-conscious intuiting and representing, as in our desiring and willing, or rather also in the representing desiring and willing (and there is no human desiring or willing without representing), that these generalities have been lifted out for themselves and, as Plato first, but then Aristotle above all did, have been made into an object of contemplation for themselves; this gives the beginning of their cognition. "Only after almost everything necessary," says Aristotle, "and what belongs to the convenience and intercourse of life, was already in existence, did men begin to strive after philosophical cognition." "In Egypt," he had remarked before, "the mathematical sciences were developed early, because the priestly caste there was early placed in a position to have leisure."

— Indeed the need to occupy oneself with pure thoughts presupposes a long course which the human spirit must have gone through; it is, one may say, the need of the already satisfied need of necessity, of needlessness to which it must have come, of abstraction from the material of intuition, of imagining and the like, of the concrete interests of desire, of the drives, of the will, in which material the determinations of thought are wrapped up.

In the quiet spaces of the thinking which has come to itself and is only in itself, the interests which move the life of peoples and individuals are silent. "After so many pages," says Aristotle in the same connection, "the nature of man is dependent; but this science, which is not sought for any use, alone is free in and for itself, and it therefore seems not to be a human possession." — Philosophy in general still has to do in its thoughts with concrete objects, God, nature, spirit, but logic concerns itself exclusively with these in themselves in their complete abstraction.

This logic is therefore usually assigned in the first place to the study of youth, who have not yet entered into the interests of concrete life, who live in leisure with a view to those interests, and who have first of all — for their subjective purpose — to occupy themselves with the acquisition of the means and of the possibility of becoming active in the objects of those interests — and with these themselves, still theoretically.

Among these means the logical science is counted, in defiance of the notion of Aristotle just cited; the occupation with it is a preliminary work, its place the school, upon which the seriousness of life and the activity for the true purposes are to follow.

In life the business is the use of the categories; they are degraded from the honour of being considered in themselves to serve in the spiritual business of living content, in the creating and the exchanging of the representations pertaining thereto — partly as abbreviations through their universality; for what an infinite multiplicity of details of external existence and activity does the representation: battle, war, people or sea, animal and the like hold together in itself; how is an infinite multiplicity of representations, activities, states and the like epitomized into the simplicity of such a representing, in the representation: God or love and the like! — partly for the closer determination and the discovery of the objective relations, in which, however, the content and the purpose, the correctness and the truth of the thinking which interferes are made wholly dependent on what is there, and no content-determining efficacy is ascribed to the determinations of thought in themselves.

Such a use of the categories, which has just been called the natural logic, is unconscious; and if in scientific reflection the relation of serving as means is imposed upon them in the mind, then thinking as such is made into something subordinated to the other spiritual determinations.

Of our feelings, drives and interests we do not readily say that they serve us, but they hold as independent forces and powers, so that we ourselves are this, so to feel, to desire and to will, to place this our interest in it.

But again, it can become more our consciousness that we stand in the service of our feelings, drives, passions and interests, and are in any case held by habit, than that we have them in our possession — still less that they, in our inner unity with them, serve us as means.

Determinations of this kind of sentiment and spirit show themselves to us now as particular in contrast to the universality of which we become conscious, in which we have our freedom, and we hold that we are rather captive in these particularities, that we are ruled by them.

Accordingly, we can hold even less that the forms of thought, which run through all our representations — be these merely theoretical or containing a material that belongs to feeling, to the drive, to the will — serve us, that we have them rather they us in our possession; what is left to us against them, how are we, I who set myself up as the more general over them, to place ourselves above them, they who are themselves the universal as such?

If we place ourselves in a feeling, a purpose, an interest and feel ourselves restricted and unfree therein, then the place into which we are able to retreat out of them and back into freedom is this place of the certainty of itself, of pure abstraction, of thinking.

Or again, if we want to speak of things, we call their nature or essence their concept, and this concept is only for thinking; but of the concepts of things we shall say even less that we master them or that the determinations of thought, of which they are the complex, serve us; on the contrary our thinking must be restricted by them, and our arbitrariness or freedom must not want to direct them after itself.

Insofar then as subjective thinking is our most own, most inward doing and the objective concept of things constitutes the thing itself, we cannot be outside that doing, cannot stand above it, and just as little can we get beyond the nature of things.

From the latter determination, however, we can abstain; it coincides with the former in so far as it would yield a relation of our thoughts to the thing, but something empty, because the thing would thereby be set up as the rule for our concepts, whereas the thing for us can be nothing other than our concepts of it.

If the critical philosophy understands the relation of these three termini in such a way that we place the thoughts between us and the things as the middle term, in the sense that this middle term rather separates us from the things instead of uniting us with them, then one must set against this view the simple observation that these very things, which are supposed to stand at the other extreme beyond us and beyond the thoughts which relate to them, are themselves thought-things and, being wholly undetermined, are only one thought-thing, — the so-called thing-in-itself of empty abstraction itself.
zh: 首先应当把这看作一个无限的进展：思维的形式从那种材料中被解放出来了，在这些材料里它们沉浸于自我意识的直观与表象，正如沉浸于我们的欲求与意愿，或者更确切地说沉浸于表象着的欲求与意愿（而没有表象，就不可能有人的欲求或意愿）；这些普遍性被为自身提升出来，并且如柏拉图首先、继而特别是亚里士多德所做的那样，被就其自身变成考察的对象；这就给出了对它们的认识的开始。「只有在几乎一切必需之物」亚里士多德说，「以及属于生活的便利与交往的东西都已经存在之后，人们才开始努力追求哲学的认识。」「在埃及，」他此前曾指出，「数学科学很早就得到了发展，因为那里的祭司阶层很早就被置于能够拥有闲暇的地位。」
——诚然，要从事纯粹思想的思考，需要预设人类精神必须走过的一段漫长历程；可以说，这是那个已经被满足的需要——对必然性的需要、对那必须达到的无所需要之需要——所产生的需要，是对撇开直观、想象等等之材料、撇开欲求与冲动与意志之具体利益的需要，而在这些材料中，思维规定正是包裹着藏着的。
在那种已经达到自身、只自在于自身的思维的静谧空间里，推动各民族与各个人生命的利益都沉默不语。「在这么多页之后，」亚里士多德在同样的关联中说，「人的本性是有依赖的；但这门不为任何用途而寻求的科学，唯独是自在自为自由的，因此它似乎并不是人的财产。」——哲学总体上仍然要在其思想中与具体的对象——上帝、自然、精神——打交道，但逻辑学只专注于这些对象在完整抽象中的自在自为。
因此，这门逻辑学通常首先成为青年的功课，因为这些青年还没有进入具体生活的利益，他们顾及着这些利益而在闲暇中生活，并且首先只是为了自己主观的目的，才不得不去获取手段以及在那些利益的客体上活动起来的可能性——从而对这些利益本身——还只是理论地——加以从事。
与亚里士多德上述的表象相抵触，逻辑科学被算作这些手段之一；对它的用力是一种预备性的工作，它的场所是学校，而生活的严肃以及对真实目的的活动的跟进，随后才应当到来。

在生活中，事情关乎范畴的运用；它们从被就其自身加以考察的荣誉上被降低下来，转而在有生命内容的精神运作中、在创造与更替相应表象的活动中效力——部分地是凭借其普遍性充当缩略词：因为「战斗」「战争」「民族或海洋」「动物」等等表象，把外在定在与活动的何等无尽的个别细节收拢在一起；而在「上帝或爱」等等表象中，又是如何把表象、活动、状态等等无尽的多种多样概括进这种表象活动的单纯性之中的！——部分地是为了更切近地规定与寻得对象的关系；但在这里，内容的充实与目的、掺入其中的思维的正确性与真理性，全都取决于现成的东西，而思维规定本身则不被赋予任何规定内容的效力。
这种范畴的运用——前面把它称作自然的逻辑学——是无意识的；而一旦在科学的反思中把「作为手段而效力」这一关系加在它们心上，那么思维本身就变成了从属于其他精神规定的东西。
对于我们的感受、冲动与利益，我们不会轻易说它们是为我们效力的；它们倒被看作独立的力量与势力，以至于我们自身就是这个：这样去感受、去欲求、去意愿，并把我们的利益置于此。
但同样地，比起我们拥有我们的感受、冲动、激情与利益，更能成为我们意识到的毋宁是：我们是处在对它们的服役之中，而且本来就受习惯支配；更不必说在我们与它们的内在统一中，它们是作为手段为我们效力了。
这类情感与精神的诸规定向我们显现出来，或者作为与那种我们据以意识到自身、并在其中拥有我们的自由普遍性相对立的特殊者；我们并认定，自己毋宁是被囚禁在这些特殊性之中，是被它们支配。
因此，我们就更不能认为，那些贯穿我们一切表象——无论这些表象只是理论的，还是包含着属于感受、冲动与意志的材料——的思维形式是在为我们效力；更不能说我们拥有它们、而非它们拥有我们；面对它们我们还剩下什么呢？我这个把自己设定为更普遍者的人，又怎能把自己置于它们之上呢——它们本身就是作为这样的普遍者。
当我们置身于某种感受、目的或利益之中，并在其中感到自己受限制、不自由时，我们能够从中脱出、退回到自由的那个场所，就是这个自身确定性的场所，就是纯粹抽象与思维的场所。
或者同样地，当我们要谈论事物时，我们把它们的自然或本质称作它们的概念，而这个概念只是为了思维而存在的；至于事物的概念，我们就更不能说我们掌握了它们，或者说构成它们之复合体的那些思维规定是为我们效力；相反，我们的思维必须受它们限制，而我们的任性或自由不应当想要按照自己的样子去支配它们。
那么，就主观思维是我们最属己、最内在的作为，而事物的客观概念就是事情本身而言，我们不能置身于那种作为之外，不能凌驾于其上；同样，我们也不能越出事物的本性。
不过，后一个规定我们可以不去管它；它与前一个规定重合，因为那只会给出我们的思想与事情之间的一种关系，但不过是空洞的，因为事情由此被立为我们的概念的法则，而事情对我们来说本来就只能是我们对它的概念。
如果批判哲学这样理解这三个项之间的关系：我们把思想置于我们与事情之间当作中项，其意义在于这个中项毋宁把我们与事情隔开，而不是把我们与它们联结起来，那么就得用一个简单的观察来反驳这种看法：这些恰恰应当站在另一极端、站在我们之外也站在那些以它们为对象的思想之外的事情，本身就是思想物，而且作为完全不确定的东西，它们只是一思想物——正是那种空洞抽象的所谓自在之物。
